::: {.section-card}
### Training duration in BUR

Duration is recorded as **`liczba_godzin`** (contact hours) for each training-service edition. The analysis covers **`Usługa szkoleniowa`** records with positive hour values.

Median duration has remained in the **low tens of hours** over the registry’s lifetime, with a long right tail driven by formal qualifications, language courses, and degree-linked programmes. The 2025 distribution is strongly concentrated in **short courses (≤40 h)**, while a minority of listings exceed **160 h** — often multi-module certificates or study programmes registered on the platform.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-block">
  <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 11.</strong> BUR training duration — median, mean and 90th percentile by year</div>
  <div id="chart-duration-yearly" class="plotly-chart plotly-chart--wide" role="img" aria-label="Training duration statistics by year in BUR"></div>
  <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> Training duration is typically short to medium, but the gap between the mean and upper percentiles indicates a long tail of more intensive programmes. This suggests that BUR mainly supports modular upskilling, with a smaller segment of longer qualification-oriented courses.</p>
</div>
<p class="notes source-note">Source: BUR yearly exports (`Usługa szkoleniowa`, positive <code>liczba_godzin</code>).</p>
```
:::

::: {.section-card}
### Duration distribution and category profiles (2025)

In 2025, the **median** training length is **26 hours** and the **90th percentile** is **82 hours**. Most subsidised services are designed as short upskilling modules rather than full qualification pathways, though a long tail of multi-module programmes remains.

Category medians vary widely: **language and IT** courses tend to be longer and more variable, while **occupational safety (BHP)** and **soft-skills** modules cluster at the short end.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-grid chart-grid--2">

    <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> The 2025 distribution confirms that most BUR training is delivered as relatively short courses. For policy, this means BUR is well suited for targeted upskilling but may be less suited, by itself, for deeper occupational transitions.</p>
  </div>
```
